narrative:
The model determined that you have a 53.4% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tips just above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. Your class ranking in the third year of law school was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Standing in the bottom decile (1 out of 10) is far below the average of roughly 6 among students who were accepted, signaling that your later academic performance raised serious concerns about passing the bar.

Your undergraduate GPA worked in the opposite direction. At 3.40 it sits above the 3.23 average of accepted students and therefore pulled the prediction toward passing, but not enough to overcome the other signals.

Your family income bracket (upper-middle) was the third most important factor and also nudged the outcome slightly toward success. However, its helpful effect was smaller than the negative impact of your third-year ranking.

Taken together, the model concluded that your academic trajectory, especially the low third-year standing, made success on the bar exam uncertain. To improve your chances, focus on raising your class rank in the remaining law school years and consider targeted bar-prep support before reapplying. This would directly address the factor that hurt your application most. (218 words)
